genericRisk: The shell is the stock pattern: four bottom tabs, a drag-to-expand sheet, iOS-style pill switches (§9.4, 5.2 x 3.2rem with a shadowed knob), full-width "Next: Colours" offers (§2.2) that read like onboarding, and #1f4f7a — the default trustworthy-app blue — as the one accent. Strip the paint words out of this document and it could be a tax app. Three specific tells: (1) the favicon (§8.6) is three rounded bars in blue/brown/green — generic chart-icon vocabulary, and green has no meaning anywhere in this app; (2) nothing in the visual language knows what watercolour is — no paper, no edge of a wash, no sense that white is the paper and not a surface (the one good instinct, --c-white meaning paper in §8.2, is never used visually); (3) --c-corporate is simultaneously the selection ring drawn over paint swatches and bars (§9.1, §9.8) — the one place colour is the subject is where the template's brand blue is laid on top of it. Second tell: hint density. Every control in §9.6 carries a permanent one- or two-line explanation. Seven of them stacked is a wall of helper copy that a painter reads once and then has to read past forever; it is the house style of generated UIs. Keep the full sentences in More settings, and give the three plan sliders a value plus at most four words.
keep: §1.1 — the diagnosis. Finding that the phone mess comes from body 1.4rem against a 16px html root, and fixing it with html { font-size: 62.5% }, is the honest root cause rather than a patch. I would defend that in any argument.
§2.2 — tabs, not a wizard, with the sliders first in the Plan step. Two taps to the slider from anywhere, nothing disabled because I skipped a step. That is how an experienced painter works.
§7.1 — sliders with a minus and plus stepper at 4.8rem, a printed value and tabular figures. First time I could set Colours to 14 exactly with a glove on instead of fighting a 14px thumb.

§5.1 and §5.2 — killing the floating recipe panel and the pointer tooltip. The panel covered the only thing I care about; the tooltip never existed on my iPad. Deleting floating.js and RecipeTip.vue outright, not fixing them, is the right call.
§10 — the table of all 34 title="" attributes with the words they become. That is the most useful page in the document and the hardest to fake.
§4.2 and §4.3 — one .colourlist row block and one .selection card for both methods, same geometry, same swatch size. Learn one, know the other. Worth the Vue awkwardness.
§9.9 — overriding a colour is a first-level action, with Back to the photo colour and Other recipes next to it. The document accepts that I will overrule the maths, which most of these apps do not.
§9.10 — the layer walk: Previous / Step 3 of 9 / Next, the three views Where to paint / This wash / So far, and Then: let it dry completely. That is shaped like actual painting.
mustFix: §3.2 against §6.7 — walk mode contradicts itself, and it contradicts itself exactly at the moment I am holding a loaded brush. §3.2 says the sheet drops to peek and "the step body shows the step instructions". §6.7 says at peek the body is height: 0; visibility: hidden. So on the phone, standing at the easel in step 3 of 9, the Mix / Paint / Then lines are both shown and hidden. Decide: give walk mode a fourth sheet height (about 20rem) that holds the wash chip and the three lines and nothing else, pinned, not collapsible, with the picture above it. Those three lines are the only text in the app I read with wet hands.

§9.10 and §14.3 — there is no way to mark anything as done, and the omission is filed as an open decision. Mix mode's whole Paint step is one Print button and a paragraph of advice. A 20-colour, 12-mix plan takes me two or three sittings; between them I have no idea where I was, and the app that made the plan is no help. Layer mode is no better: §10 states plainly "Ticks only change what the picture shows." Specify a tick per mix and per layer step that means painted, persisted in the collection record with the picture, shown in the Colours list and in the walk bar. Without it the Paint step is not a step, it is a print dialog.

§9.10 — "Paint the biggest areas first: colour 1 covers the most of the picture." That is wrong, printed as instruction, in the step where I am about to commit paint. In watercolour I go light to dark; if the biggest area is my darkest mix I have ruined the sheet before the second wash. It is doubly wrong because §9.8 orders the list by share of image, so number 1 is the largest area, not the lightest wash. Order the mix list light to dark by value (you already have the mix hex), keep the share percentage in the row because it tells me how much to mix, and change the sentence to light to dark, lightest first, with the darks and the small strong touches last. Layer mode already gets this right — mix mode must not teach the opposite.

§9.7 — zoom is removed outright and the picture numbers are left unreadable. "Zoom-to-fit is removed as a control entirely: the picture is always fitted to its band." On the phone band that is roughly 390 px wide, and PaintingCanvas.vue draws the area labels through labelFont() at a fixed size on an upscaled buffer which is then CSS-fitted down — so 6L in a small area is a smudge, and MIN_LABEL_DIST drops the labels in narrow areas altogether. The brief's first question is whether I can see which colour number 7 is. The answer here is no, and the document removes the only control that helped. The close-up is not a substitute: it re-analyses, it becomes a numbered detail I later have to delete through the Remove… toggle in §7.3, and all I wanted was to look. Add two-finger pinch and pan inside the picture band (the band is a known height, so this costs no reflow) and specify a minimum on-screen label size with a fallback: when labels would fall below about 11 px on screen, number only the areas with room and say so in the readout.

§5.2 — the readout carries the most important sentence in the app and is specified as its smallest, faintest, most truncated text. min-height 2.4rem, --fs-small (1.3rem on the phone), --c-copy-light, white-space: nowrap, text-overflow: ellipsis — one line. "Colour 6L — 2 x 663 Sepia brown + 1 x 498 Delft blue — 12 % of the image" does not fit in 358 px at 13 px; I get the first four words. The same line is also the only channel for analysis.error in §5.3, so a failure arrives greyed out and cut in half. Give the readout two lines (min-height 4.8rem, no nowrap), set it at --fs-copy in --c-copy, and keep --c-copy-light only for the idle mode hint. Under a studio lamp or in daylight on the terrace, copy-light at 13 px is not text, it is texture.

§2.5 and §5.3 — the destructive things sit in the row I touch constantly, and nothing in the document confirms or undoes. The Photo step puts Choose a photo, Take a photo, Next sample, Save to collection and Collection in one button group (library.css). Next sample throws away the whole plan including every colour I changed by hand, and it is 0.8rem from Save to collection. There is no confirm anywhere in the specification except the paint box's two-press delete (§12), and no undo at all. Worse: the paint box (§9.6, a .button--secondary --block in the Plan step, and again in the Colours step header) re-mixes every recipe when I press Update mixes or Auto, which silently discards every hand override — the document never says so. Specify: Next sample and Choose a photo ask once when there are unsaved hand-changed colours; Update mixes and Auto name the count ("4 colours you changed by hand will be mixed again") before they run; move Next sample out of the save/collection row and give the sample control its own line.

§3.1 — "Tapping the picture always moves the steps surface to Colours and raises it to half." On a phone, 46dvh of sheet comes up over the lower half of the picture, which is often the half I just tapped, and the sheet is an overlay so the picture does not move out from under it (§6.3). Asking about four areas in a row means four cover-ups and four grip taps to get back. The readout already answers the question (§5.2 rule 6). Raise only to a short selection height, about 16rem, that shows the swatch pair, the recipe line and Change colour, and let the painter raise it further if they want Other recipes. Never cover the tapped point without being asked.

§9.2 against §8.2 — the primary button is unreadable in dark mode. .button--primary is background: var(--c-corporate); colour: var(--c-white), and dark mode flips --c-corporate to #8db9dd, a pale blue, while the text stays white. That is about 2:1. Print or save a PDF and Paint step by step are the two primary buttons in the app, and in the evening both vanish. Dark mode needs its own primary pairing: keep #8db9dd as the fill and set the label to --c-background (#171614), or add a token for the on-primary text and define it per theme.

§6.3 and §9.7 — the phone view bar does not fit and hides real controls behind a horizontal scroll. Four .segmented__option at min-width 7.2rem is 288 px, plus Show (4.8rem), plus a Zoom in on a part button with white-space: nowrap at roughly 15 rem, inside about 326 px of usable width — around 180 px overflows, and §9.3 answers it with .segmented--scroll and scrollbar-width: none. So Sketch, the view I need to trace the drawing, and the framing button are off the right edge with no visible hint, in a 5.6rem strip that is also easy to swipe by accident while reaching for the picture. State what is visible without scrolling on a phone: put the four views on their own full-width row, and Show plus Zoom in on a part on the row below, or make the views two rows of two. No primary control may need a sideways swipe to be discovered.
shouldFix: §6.4 against §6.7 — the sheet peek height for tablet portrait is 8.8rem in the §6.4 table and 10.4rem in §6.7. Pick one; the step bar's visibility at peek depends on it.

§10 and §4.3 — software noise promoted from tooltip to first level. "Match: excellent (2.4)" prints a raw colour distance next to a word that already says it, and the layer row meta gains "brings 1.3 closer". 1.3 of what? I have never mixed 1.3 of anything. Delete both numbers and keep the words. The brief asked what I would never look at; those are it. Keep "13 % of the picture is out of reach of these paints" and "31 separate shapes in this step" — those two change what I do.

§8.4 — the typeface justification rests on a claim that is wrong. IBM Plex Sans's capital I is a bare stem and its lowercase l has no tail; the crossbars and the tail belong to IBM Plex Mono. The rejection of Inter is argued on exactly that point, so the comparison collapses. The real argument for Plex here is figures, not letters: I read 663, 498, 208 and 526 all day, and 663 against 668 at --fs-mini inside a 2.0rem recipe bar is the hard case. Redo the justification on digit pairs with tabular figures at the actual sizes, printed and held at arm's length, and say which of Plex, Inter and Atkinson won on the sheet.

§9.12 and §12 — the printed sheet, the one thing that comes to the wet table and survives, is the only part not designed. "Unchanged except class prefix and tokens. Must keep printing identically" cannot both be true: the base size, the typeface and every token change. Specify the sheet properly — the area number as the largest thing on it, the recipe in words and ratios, paint numbers in tabular figures, and no reliance on a home printer's colour fidelity for the swatch, which it will get wrong. Say in print what the swatch is only an indication of.

§7.1 — nothing says what happens to the stepper while an analysis is running. "Every change re-analyses" (§3), and the only busy treatment is a dimmed picture (§9.1). Four impatient taps on + with a glove queue four analyses. Specify that taps coalesce to the last value and that the control stays tappable, never disabled — a control that goes dead under my finger is worse than a slow one.

§6.7 — the grip tap cycles peek, half, full, back to peek. Coming down from full I lose the list entirely and have to tap again to get back to half. Make the tap toggle between peek and the last raised height, and keep the drag for the third.

§9.8 — the wash key (L light, M medium, R rich, S strong) appears "only when a mix has more than one wash", yet single-wash rows still print "light" in their meta. Then the word has no legend on screen. Show the key whenever any wash word is printed, and repeat it on the printed sheet.

§6 — nothing says what happens when I turn the iPad, which I do constantly. Rail becomes sheet and back: state whether the open step survives, what the sheet height becomes, what happens to an open More settings, and whether the Show popover becomes the inline switches mid-session.

§9.6 — Paint box sits on the Plan step's first level, directly above More settings, styled .button--secondary --block, with no warning that it is the control which re-does every recipe in the picture. It belongs under its own small heading ("The paints you own") with the count of selected paints printed next to it, so I can see the state without opening it.

§7.3 — the Remove… / Done toggle is a good idea, but it is specified only for the close-up tiles. Collection delete and own-paint delete (§12) use a different two-press pattern. One deletion pattern for the whole app, stated once.
verdict: This is the first version of this app written by someone who looked at where the pain actually is, and it is still not a plan I would put paint on good paper with. The diagnosis in §1 is honest, the four tabs are right, the sliders finally have steppers, and the floating panel and the pointer tooltip are rightly killed rather than patched. Then the document stops being about painting. The step where I actually paint (§9.10) is a print button, a paragraph of advice and one sentence of advice that is wrong for watercolour; nothing anywhere can be marked as done, and that omission is written off as a question for round 2. Walk mode tells itself to show and to hide the instructions in the same breath (§3.2 against §6.7), so the one screen I read with a wet brush is undefined. I cannot magnify the picture at all any more (§9.7), on a phone where the numbers are already too small to read. The sentence that tells me what a colour is made of is set in the smallest, palest, truncated-to-one-line text in the app (§5.2). And the control that discards an hour of hand-corrected colours sits a finger's width from Save, with no confirm and no undo anywhere in the document. Fix those six and this becomes a tool. As written it is a well-organised settings screen with a picture at the top.

genericRisk: Low on the usual tells — no purple, no glass, no pill soup, no emoji, and §8.7 keeps icons to five places. The risk is a different kind of default: the spec is a *handsome document* more than a *tested design*. Three symptoms. (1) It carries the current build's defects across under new names: `--c-selected` reproducing `--accent-soft`'s two meanings, and `--c-white` on `--c-corporate` reproducing today's dark-mode `#fff` on `#8fb6dc` — a rename that preserves the bug is the signature of a redesign done in a text editor. (2) The sheet geometry (§6.7) and the "slider above the fold at every breakpoint" claim (§2.2) are stated confidently and both fail the arithmetic in the spec's own numbers, which means no one laid the bands out at 390x844 before writing the sentence. (3) The IBM Plex justification (§8.4) is the best-written section in the document and the one with zero consequences for the user's hands — effort went where it reads well. The four-tab bottom sheet with a grip and peek/half/full is also the single most-generated mobile pattern of the last five years; it is the right pattern here, but §6.7 should say *why* three heights rather than two, since nothing in the content inventory needs three and each extra height is a state the painter has to learn with wet hands.
keep: §1.1, the root-cause diagnosis. `--font-size: 1.4rem` in `_variables.css` on a default-16px `html` really is the whole screenshot — I checked `src/css/base/_reset.css:3`. Every other symptom in `phone-settings-2026-10-12.png` falls out of it. The `62.5%` fix is also better than it claims: because every band height in §6.3/§6.4 is in `rem`, the whole frame scales with the user's browser font size instead of breaking at it.

§4.1, three fixed slots that do not reflow when the method is switched. This is the one structural decision that directly kills the class of bug in the evidence image, and it costs nothing. Keep the rule that the panel never changes shape, even if the labels and ranges change.

§5.1 and §5.2, deleting `floating.js` and `RecipeTip.vue`. Both are real files, both depend on a pointer, and the reasons given (covers the subject, 1px drag handle, positions persisted per device so a panel parked on a laptop reappears wrong on the iPad) are the right reasons in the right order. Do not reopen this in round 2.

§10's instrument — a table of every `title` with a named destination — is the correct way to discharge the hover ban. It is incomplete (see must-fix), but the method is right and the destinations it does name are specific text, not 'becomes visible'.
§7.2, the tap fallback for close-up framing, reusing the 'too small a frame' branch `endFrame` already has. Cheap, correct, and it turns today's silent no-op into an action.
§3.1, exactly one automatic navigation (tap the picture, go to Colours), stated as a rule and argued. Resist adding a second one in round 2.

§14.4, honestly recording that the brief's inventory names All/Invert/None while `PaintBox.vue` only has Auto, Revert and Clear. I checked; the spec is right and the brief is wrong. That is the behaviour you want from a round-1 document.
mustFix: §6.7 and §2.1 contradict each other, and §6.7 loses. `--sheet-full: calc(100dvh - 20rem)` leaves 200px above the sheet; the phone bands in §6.3 above it are top bar 5.6rem + view bar 5.6rem + readout 2.4rem = 136px, so the picture band is 64px, and `.picture { padding: var(--gap) }` eats 32 of those. With the close-up bar present (4.8rem) the band is 16px — less than zero picture. So the sentence 'The sheet never becomes a full-screen takeover: the picture stays visible at every height' is false on the primary phone, and §2.1's 'Always on screen, at every breakpoint' with it. Fix in §6.7: set `--sheet-full` from the chrome, e.g. `calc(100dvh - var(--chrome-top) - 24rem)` with `--chrome-top` summing the bands actually rendered, and state a floor for the picture band (say 18rem) that the sheet may never cross. Same arithmetic on tablet portrait: 48dvh/`100dvh - 24rem` leaves 96px of an 834x1194 iPad's picture at full against §6.4's own 32dvh minimum.

Dark mode fails contrast on the most-used control in the app. §8.2 sets `--c-corporate: #8db9dd` and §9.2 keeps `.button--primary { background: var(--c-corporate); colour: var(--c-white) }` — white on #8db9dd is 2.1:1, far under 4.5:1, and it is the Print button, the Paint step by step button and the Continue button in `AccountGate`. §9.4's `.switch--tick` checked state has the same problem: a `--c-white` layer number on `#8db9dd`. §8.2 even states the principle ('`--c-white` … never for a surface') and then §9.2 breaks it. Fix: add `--c-on-corporate` to the token set, `#ffffff` light and `#13212c` dark, and use it for every foreground that sits on `--c-corporate`. While you are there, put the computed ratio next to each pair in §8.1/§8.2 — the spec quotes no contrast figure anywhere.

The readout (§5.2) is the app's only status channel and it is specified as a single clipped line with no programmatic equivalent. §9.7 gives it `min-height: 2.4rem; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis` at `--fs-small` (1.3rem on a phone). The real strings do not fit 358px: the store's own error is `Could not load image: the file is not a picture this browser can read` (`analysis.js:297`), and rule 5's mix sentence is `Colour 6L — 2 x 663 Sepia brown + 1 x 498 Delft blue — 12 % of the image`. Both arrive truncated at exactly the moment they matter. Worse, the error is distinguished from ordinary status by `--c-danger` alone — colour carrying meaning, and against the owner's own 'status in words' rule. Fix in §5.2: allow the readout two lines on phone and tablet portrait (`min-height: 2.4rem`, no `nowrap`, `max-height: 2 lines`), prefix errors with the word `Problem:` and busy with `Working:`, add `aria-live="polite"` (`assertive` for errors) and `role="status"`, and give the error a visible dismiss — `analysis.error` only clears on the next load or analysis, so a stuck error permanently occupies the line that is supposed to show recipes.

On a phone the painter can no longer make the picture bigger. §9.7 removes the fit/full-size control outright, `.picture__canvas` gets `touch-action: manipulation`, `.app` is `overflow: hidden` and the page never scrolls — so there is no pinch, no pan and no full-size view. The argued replacement, the close-up, costs a re-analysis and creates a stored detail. The brief's phone scenario is 'the painter checks a colour on the phone while the picture is on the easel'; checking a colour in a 390x~250px band of a photo is the task, and the design has removed every way to magnify. Fix §9.7: keep the picture band pinch-zoomable and pannable (`touch-action: none` with pointer handling in `PaintingCanvas.vue`, a double-tap-free reset button in the view bar labelled `Fit the picture`), or restore a full-size overlay on phone and tablet portrait. Removing the control is defensible on the iPad in landscape; it is not defensible on the screen this rework exists to fix.

§7.1's steppers specify one analysis per tap: 'they change the value by `step` and call the same `@change` handler the slider calls, so an analysis runs once per tap.' `ControlsPanel.vue` binds `@change="analysis.analyse()"` on all seven ranges. Going from Colours 8 to 20 is twelve taps and twelve full worker analyses, each dimming the canvas to `opacity: 0.55` and flipping the readout to `Analysing…`. The steppers are also the only way to set an exact value with gloves, because the phone track is ~246px wide for a 2–32 range, about 7px per step. Fix §7.1: the stepper writes the value and the readout immediately and commits the analysis after ~400ms of no further taps (and on press-and-hold repeat, once at the end). State it as a rule, not an implementation note — this is the difference between the steppers being usable and being a trap.

§10 claims to list 'every one of them' and states 34 occurrences; the code has 33 and the table misses three of them, in two files the table never names. `AiPanel.vue:13` (`:title="choice.title"` — 'The app chooses colours and paints itself' / 'An AI model chooses colours and paints, once you ask it') and, more seriously, `LayerSteps.vue:22`, the walk-mode view switch: 'Where to paint' = 'The paper after this step; what is painted now in full colour, the rest faded', 'This wash' = 'Only the areas painted now, filled with one stroke of this wash', 'So far' = 'The paper with all layers up to and including this step'. §9.10 draws that three-way control with its labels and never says where the explanations go — so the one screen where the painter is standing with a wet brush loses all three. (`LayerSteps.vue:31`'s swatch caveat is also unlisted; its twin from `LayerList` is handled.) Fix: add the rows, and in §9.10 put the three sentences under the walk bar as the `.field__hint` of the chosen view, the way §9.6 does for Method.

Nothing in the design says what a free account sees before or after it hits a limit. `pro.require()` gates printing (`ControlsPanel.vue:302`), the eighth paint (`PaintBox.vue:197`, `FREE_PAINTS = 8`), a second box and saving (`collection.js:41`, `FREE_IMAGES = 0` in the browser). The spec gives `Print or save a PDF` as the Paint step's `.button--primary` with no locked state, `.chip--paint` with no unavailable state, and §9.12 defers `ProDialog` entirely. And on a phone every dialog is `width: 100vw; height: 100dvh` (§9.11), so `ProDialog` opens over a full-screen `PaintBox` — `CollectionDialog.vue:76` already closes itself to avoid this and `PaintBox` does not. Fix: add a `--locked` modifier to §9.2 and §9.11 (the control stays visible, keeps its size per §9.1, and carries a visible word such as `Full version`), name the stacking rule for a dialog opening over a full-screen dialog, and specify where `account.notice` renders — `App.vue:10` shows it today and §12's App.vue row does not mention it at all.
shouldFix: §9.2 and §9.1 give `--c-selected` two jobs: `.button--secondary` background and the selected/pressed state, separated only by a 2px inset ring. This reproduces exactly the confusion in the evidence image, where `--accent-soft` makes 'New' and 'Take photo' look as selected as 'Mix' and 'Organic' (`_button.css` uses it for both). Give `.button--secondary` its own neutral fill (`--c-surface-sunk` with `--c-copy`) and reserve `--c-selected` for on-states.

The 0.8rem gap rule in §7 is contradicted by the two controls a gloved hand uses most. §6.8's `.steps` is a bare flex row of four tabs with no gap, and §9.3's `.segmented__option` are flush by design. Either state the exemption and compensate (raise `.segmented__option` and `.steps__tab` to a 7.2rem minimum width and widen the 1px divider's visual separation), or add separation. Mis-tapping Mix for Layer re-runs the whole plan.

§6.3's view bar does not fit a phone. `.segmented__option { min-width: 7.2rem }` x four views = 288px, plus the `Show` button and `Zoom in on a part` (a full-word label) against ~358px of usable width. §9.3's `.segmented--scroll` hides the scrollbar (`scrollbar-width: none`), so `Sketch` — the view the painter needs to trace outlines onto paper — sits off-screen with no indication it exists. Specify an edge fade or a visible overflow affordance, or move `Show` and `Zoom in on a part` out of that row on phone.

§4.2 and §9.8 never state the real row height. `min-height: 7.2rem` is given, then a recipe bar (2.0rem) and a wash bar (3.2rem, padded to 4.8rem) are drawn 'full width under the row'. Is 7.2rem the whole row or the top line? It decides whether a phone sheet at `half` shows three mixes or one, which is the central phone question for a 12-mix list. State the composed height and how many rows are visible at peek, half and full.

§3.1 raises the sheet to `half` on a tap, which on a phone is 46dvh of overlay rising over the bottom of the picture — frequently over the very area the painter just tapped, hiding the selection highlight that confirms what was selected. Specify that the canvas re-centres the selected region into the band above the sheet, or cap the automatic rise so the tapped point stays visible.

No focus management anywhere. §9.1 gives a focus-visible ring and that is the whole of it: nothing on tab order, on what receives focus when a step changes, when the sheet opens, when a dialog opens or closes and where focus returns, or how the `More` menu and `Show` popover dismiss on Escape. §9.11's dialogs are `<dialog>`, which gives a trap for free, but the sheet and the popover are not. One short section would close this.

Screen-reader semantics are absent for the colour list specifically, and the design makes them worse than today. §10 deletes the wash `title` ('6L: medium, 12% of image') and the bar-part `title` ('1.5 x 663 Sepia brown'), replacing them with 'the readout prints the full sentence on selection' — the readout being visual and clipped. A screen-reader user is left with a button named 'L'. Specify the list markup (`ul`/`li`, the row as a button with a composed accessible name: 'Mix 2, 663 Sepia brown and 498 Delft blue, 14 per cent of the picture, 3 washes'), and give the wash buttons a full `aria-label`. Likewise §7.1's stepper labels 'Fewer' and 'More' appear seven times on one screen; make them 'Fewer colours', 'More colours'.

The word 'Colours' carries four meanings at once: the step tab (§2.2), the step body title (§8.3), the list header 'Colours 20 in 12 mixes' (§9.8) and the Plan slider that sets how many there are (§9.6). Layer mode repeats the collision with 'Layers'. Rename one side — the slider to `How many colours` / `How many layers`, or the step to `Palette` / `Plan of layers`.

The paint box phone screen is not designed. §9.11 gives a full-screen shell and `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(16rem, 1fr))`, which at 358px is two columns; 54 paints at `5.6rem` is roughly 1500px of scrolling with no search, no sticky group headers and no count of what is selected (`PaintBox.vue` has no filter today). Specify the phone layout: a sticky selected-count line, sticky `Pans` / `Tubes` / `Your own paints` headers, and a filter field, or say explicitly that finding one paint among 54 by scrolling is accepted and why.

§6.1 has no place for a phone in landscape. `(min-width: 600px) and (max-width: 1023px)` catches a 844x390 iPhone and hands it the tablet-portrait frame: 6.4rem top bar + 5.6rem view bar + 2.4rem readout + 10.4rem peek = 248 of 390px before any picture. Add an `(orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 500px)` branch, even if its content is just 'short top bar, no readout, sheet at peek only'.

Spec-quality nits that cost an implementer time: §6.2 gives `.app` two grid rows while §6.3 lists six bands and never defines the phone `.app__main` grid (only §6.5 defines one, for landscape). §7.1's thumb `margin-top: -1.1rem` should be -1.0rem to centre a 3.2rem thumb on a 1.2rem track. §7.1 tells Firefox to paint the `--fill` gradient on `::-moz-range-track` ('same as the webkit track') *and* to paint `::-moz-range-progress`, which double-paints. §9.4's `.switch__input` is `position: absolute` with no positioned ancestor declared on `.switch`.
verdict: A strong, unusually honest document that is about one revision short of buildable — and it is weakest on the screen it was written to rescue. The diagnosis in §1 is correct down to the line of CSS, §4's unification of mix and layer mode is the right structural idea, and §5's deletion of the floating panel and the pointer tooltip is argued rather than asserted. But the phone is specified in bands and token values rather than laid out: §6.7's own numbers put 16–64px of picture behind a full sheet while the same section promises the picture is never covered; §9.7 removes every way to magnify the photo on the one device where the band is smallest; §5.2 funnels every error, every status and every recipe into a 24px clipped single line with no live region and with errors marked by colour alone. Dark mode ships a 2.1:1 primary button because the spec renamed the current build's defect instead of fixing it. The claim I would press hardest in an argument is §10's — 'every one of them' is three short, and one of the misses takes all three explanations off the walk-mode view switch, in layer mode, on a phone, with a wet brush in hand. Round 2 does not need a different design; it needs the author to open a 390x844 window, set the sheet to full, and read what they wrote.
